name: FX volatility carry trade
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Selling Currency Volatility Premium
caseLead: Currency option sellers can earn premiums when realised exchange rate moves remain smaller than those priced into options. Demand from companies and investors hedging currency exposure can keep option premiums elevated, particularly when central bank decisions or political developments create exchange rate uncertainty.
caseRest: A sudden currency move can generate losses far larger than the premiums collected, particularly after an unexpected central bank decision. Such moves often follow central bank decisions, such as the Swiss National Bank's removal of its exchange rate floor in January 2015, and can leave no time to adjust hedges. Rehyn estimates that a single episode can erase many months of premium, so the strategy's smooth monthly returns understate the risk of rare losses.
figNote: Each card shows the move in the main exchange rate from its level before the event to its low or high during the episode. Currency option sellers earn premium when moves are small and lose when the exchange rate moves by more than the options imply.

events.title: ECB pledge to defend the euro calms markets
events.text: ECB President Mario Draghi pledged on 26 July 2012 to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro, and the euro rose about 2% against the US dollar. The strategy gained because implied volatility fell as the threat of a breakup receded.

events.title: Swiss National Bank removes the franc floor
events.text: The Swiss National Bank removed its floor of 1.20 francs per euro on 15 January 2015, and the euro fell as much as 29% against the franc. The strategy lost because the exchange rate moved far beyond the range priced into options.

events.title: UK vote to leave the European Union
events.text: The UK vote of 23 June 2016 to leave the European Union cut the pound's value against the US dollar by about 11% within hours. The strategy lost because the move was far larger than the daily range priced into options.

events.title: Catalan vote leaves the euro little changed
events.text: The Catalan independence vote and the Spanish government's response in October 2017 raised political risk in Europe, yet the euro fell only about 1% against the US dollar. The strategy gained because the premium on euro options was larger than the movement that followed.

events.title: Bank of Japan rate rise unwinds yen trades
events.text: A Bank of Japan rate rise forced yen-funded trades to close, and the US dollar fell about 12% against the yen from its July high to 5 August 2024. Results were mixed because a rebound over the following weeks recovered part of the loss.

events.title: US tariffs trigger a slide in the dollar
events.text: The April 2025 announcement of sweeping US tariffs led investors to sell dollar assets, and the euro rose about 6% against the US dollar within three weeks. The strategy lost because realised volatility in the main pairs rose above the level priced into options.

instrument: Options on G10 currency pairs, mainly EUR/USD, USD/JPY and GBP/USD; one to three months to expiry; hedged daily in spot
rules: Strangles sold when one-month implied volatility exceeds realised volatility by at least 1.5 points; wings bought against tail moves; positions delta hedged each day
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads on options and spot hedges deducted at each trade
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from volatility premium to tail protection

legs.purpose: Earns the premium priced into currency volatility
Limits losses when an exchange rate gaps
Removes directional exposure to the exchange rate
Provides collateral and earns the cash rate

entry: One-month implied volatility at least 1.5 points above realised volatility
size: Set to a 6% annualised volatility target; no single pair above 40% of risk
exit: Closed at 60% of premium collected, or 10 days before expiry
stop: A pair is closed if it moves by more than three daily standard deviations in one day
marketWatch: The gap between implied and realised volatility in the main currency pairs is the main indicator for this strategy now. Central bank decisions, trade announcements and political votes matter because exchange rates can move by more than the options imply in a single session. Rehyn also watches positioning in funding currencies, since a rapid unwinding of carry trades has produced the largest moves.

favourable.heading: Central bank backstops reduce volatility
favourable.text: Credible central bank support favours the strategy because it lowers the chance of large moves and lets implied volatility fall. After President Draghi's pledge in July 2012, the euro rose only about 2% against the US dollar and option prices declined.

favourable.heading: Political risk with contained moves
favourable.text: Political tension that stays within a narrow range favours the strategy because option buyers pay for protection that is not used. Around the Catalan independence vote in October 2017, the euro fell only about 1% against the US dollar.

favourable.heading: Range-bound markets with stable policy
favourable.text: Stable monetary policy favours the strategy because exchange rates then stay inside the range implied by options. Much of 2017 and 2019 followed this pattern, with EUR/USD implied volatility near multi-year lows.

adverse.heading: Central bank policy reversals
adverse.text: A sudden change in central bank policy hurts the strategy because the exchange rate can gap before option sellers adjust hedges. In January 2015 the euro fell as much as 29% against the Swiss franc after the Swiss National Bank removed its floor.

adverse.heading: Binary political outcomes
adverse.text: Political votes with a clear either-or result hurt the strategy because the exchange rate moves in one step rather than gradually. After the UK referendum in June 2016 the pound fell about 11% against the US dollar within hours.

adverse.heading: Forced unwinding of carry positions
adverse.text: Rapid unwinding of currency carry positions hurts the strategy because borrowed currencies rise quickly when investors close trades together. In August 2024 the US dollar fell about 12% against the yen from its July high to 5 August as yen-funded positions were closed.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, using monthly G10 currency option returns including delta hedging. Each event window runs from the last strategy high before the shock to the subsequent low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in G10 exchange rates and implied currency volatility, which are then applied to the strategy's current option positions.
